vitrina_lrv: Can you imagine driving a car on the Moon? This is the moon buggy {directo}, the Apollo 17 lunar vehicle. In 1972 {exacto} the astronauts used it to explore the surface, and it's still there, more than 50 years later! Do you want to discover its story {cercano}? Clap hard to start the interaction!
vitrina_cassini: Did you know a spacecraft spent thirteen years orbiting Saturn? This is the Cassini probe {directo}. It reached Saturn in 2004 {exacto} and carried the Huygens probe, which landed on Titan, Saturn's largest moon, in 2005. In 2017 it ended its mission by diving into the planet {cercano}, so it wouldn't contaminate its moons.
regreso_museo: Great tour {cercano}! When the mission is ready, you'll be able to live it in full!
ayuda: Raise your knees: walk · tilt your head: turn · point at a showcase for 1.5 s · clap hard: enter or board the moon buggy · thumb and index finger together: grab · hold a closed fist in the mission: back to the museum · OK sign with both hands: get off the moon buggy
calibracion_instruccion: Look straight ahead, keep your head still and your hands relaxed.
luna_entrando_museo: Welcome to the Apollo 17 simulation! It's 1972, in the Taurus-Littrow valley, next to the Challenger lunar module. See that compartment? The moon buggy is stored in there, completely folded! Your first mission is to deploy it. Hold your fist closed to do it!
luna_lejos_LRV: You're too far away, explorer! Get closer to the moon buggy and clap hard to climb aboard.
luna_sentado_en_LRV: Lunar pilot on board! Hold the wheel with both hands and raise your knees to drive, and make the OK sign with both hands to get off. To climb aboard, clap hard. In real life the orange soil was much farther away, but here it's much closer. Your mission: find the orange soil, the one with the blue halo, and collect a sample. Light up your explorer spirit and let's go!
luna_sentado_en_LRV_teclado: Lunar pilot on board! Use W, A, S and D to drive and B to get off. To climb aboard, press space. In real life the orange soil was much farther away, but here it's much closer. Your mission: find the orange soil, the one with the blue halo, and collect a sample. Light up your explorer spirit and let's go!
luna_cerca_de_roca: Target located! That's the famous orange soil! Strike it with the hammer to get a sample: bring your hand down fast!
luna_golpeando: Nice hit, explorer! Now collect the sample: bring your thumb and index finger together!
luna_golpe_fallido: Oops, so close! The Moon isn't going anywhere. Get closer and try again.
luna_bajado: Boots on lunar soil! You got off the moon buggy: walk by raising your knees to explore. To climb back aboard, get close and clap hard.
luna_bajado_muestra: Sample secured! You're carrying a clue to the Moon's ancient volcanic eruptions. Hold your fist closed to return to the museum and continue the adventure!
opc_suavizado: Cursor smoothing (0.05 very smooth · 1 no filter)
opc_tiempo_oculta_mano: Seconds without seeing the hand before it disappears
opc_umbral_salto_mano: Maximum jump to glide when it reappears (m)
saludo_bienvenida: Hello, {nombre}! I'm Robi, your space guide in this museum of the future.
saludo_vitrinas: Whenever you're ready, select one of the showcases by pointing at it with your finger to begin the immersion.
saludo_vitrinas_teclado: Whenever you're ready, click and hold one of the showcases to begin the immersion.
inicio_elige: How do you want to explore the museum?
inicio_control_camara_desc: Walk by raising your knees, turn by tilting your head and point with your finger. Needs a webcam.
inicio_control_teclado_desc: W A S D to walk, mouse to look around and click to point. Doesn't use the camera.
inicio_camara_fallo: Couldn't use the camera ({error}). You can play with keyboard and mouse, or try the camera again.
inicio_lema: Walk among rockets, probes and planets, and set foot on the Moon with Apollo 17. The universe is waiting for you.
inicio_idioma_pregunta: Nice to meet you, {nombre}. Which language shall we travel in?
ayuda_teclado: W A S D: walk · mouse: look · hold click on a showcase for 1.5 s · space: enter or board the moon buggy · E again: grab · hold E in a mission: back to the museum · B: get off the moon buggy · Esc: options
teclado_clic_mirar: Click on the scene to look around with the mouse.
opc_cambiar_control: Change control (returns to the start screen)
luna_entrando_museo_teclado: Welcome to the Apollo 17 simulation! It's 1972, in the Taurus-Littrow valley, next to the Challenger lunar module. See that compartment? The moon buggy is stored in there, completely folded! Your first mission is to deploy it. Hold down the E key to do it!
luna_lejos_LRV_teclado: You're too far away, explorer! Get closer to the moon buggy and press space to climb aboard.
luna_cerca_de_roca_teclado: Target located! That's the famous orange soil! Strike it with the hammer to get a sample: click!
luna_suelo_recogido: You did it, explorer! Why is this orange soil so special? It contains tiny spheres of volcanic glass, formed about 3.5 billion years ago. Proof that the Moon had volcanic activity! The moon buggy was also key: it let the astronauts travel up to 8.7 km from the lunar module and reach this crater.
luna_golpeando_teclado: Nice hit, explorer! Now collect the sample: click again!
luna_bajado_teclado: Boots on lunar soil! You got off the moon buggy: walk with W to explore. To climb back aboard, get close and press space.
luna_bajado_muestra_teclado: Sample secured! You're carrying a clue to the Moon's ancient volcanic eruptions. Hold down the E key to return to the museum and continue the adventure!
luna_mantener_E: Hold E to deploy the moon buggy!
luna_LRV_plegado: Hold on, explorer! The moon buggy is still folded. Hold your fist closed to deploy it!
luna_LRV_plegado_teclado: Hold on, explorer! The moon buggy is still folded. Hold down the E key to deploy it!
luna_despliegue_liberacion: The deployment begins! Schmitt releases the moon buggy from the ladder and Cernan tilts it outward by pulling a tape. Watch it start to unfold!
luna_despliegue_chasis: Watch it transform! As it tilts 45 degrees, the rear chassis opens and its wheels snap into place. Now the front part unfolds!
luna_despliegue_bajada: Schmitt pulls the other tape to lower the front part. They remove the pins and separate the moon buggy from the module! It's now on the lunar ground!
luna_despliegue_preparacion: Almost ready! They extend the fenders, raise the seats and lower the console. The moon buggy is taking shape!
luna_despliegue_prueba: Time to put it to the test! Cernan powers it up and checks that it can move forward and turn. Everything works!
luna_despliegue_carga: Final preparations! They install the radio, the antennas, the camera and the tools. The moon buggy is ready to explore!
luna_LRV_desplegado: Mission accomplished! The moon buggy is ready to explore. Now it's your turn to drive! Get close and clap hard to climb aboard.
luna_LRV_desplegado_teclado: Mission accomplished! The moon buggy is ready to explore. Now it's your turn to drive! Get close and press space to climb aboard.
pres_intro: Meet the Apollo moon buggy! {@nombre}Its real name is Lunar Roving Vehicle: {@electrico}an electric vehicle designed to explore the Moon. {@astronautas}It was used by the astronauts of Apollo 15, 16 and 17.
pres_chasis: How do you fit a vehicle inside a spacecraft? By making it foldable! {@chasis}The chassis, the structure that holds the whole moon buggy together, folds to fit in a compartment of the lunar module. {@ingenieria}A brilliant engineering solution!
pres_ruedas: These wheels have no air and never go flat! {@malla}Their steel wire mesh absorbs the bumps, while {@chevrones}the titanium treads give them grip on the lunar dust. {@disenadas}Designed to roll on another world!
pres_peso: On the Moon it weighs six times less! On Earth it weighs 460 pounds, but there only 76.
pres_consola: The console shows the moon buggy's driving data!
pres_comunicaciones: And thanks to its {@camara}television camera and its {@antenas}antennas, Earth could follow the adventure! {@tierra}The images and signals traveled all the way to our planet.
pres_mando_movimientos: Forget the steering wheel and pedals! {@palanca}The moon buggy was driven with a single lever: {@adelante}forward to accelerate, {@lados}to the sides to turn {@atras}and back to brake. {@marcha}And to reverse? {@interruptor}You flip a switch {@reversa}and move the lever back!
pres_cierre: On Apollo 17, the moon buggy took the astronauts to {@suelo}the orange soil, volcanic material from the Moon! An incredible discovery.
pres_listo: Now you know the secrets of the moon buggy! Are you ready for the mission?
opc_subtitulos_lrv: Subtitles in the moon buggy animation
pres_distancias: Walking on the Moon in a heavy spacesuit was not easy at all! {@buggy}Thanks to the moon buggy, the astronauts could explore much greater distances, covering tens of kilometers on wheels.
pres_navegacion: Driving on the Moon was quite a challenge! {@nav}With no GPS, a gyroscope {@vueltas}and the turns of its wheels helped them know where they were.
pres_energia: {@recarga}And where do you recharge a vehicle on the Moon? Nowhere! That's why the moon buggy carried {@baterias}silver-zinc batteries to power its electric motors. {@mylar}And that golden covering? It's Mylar, part of its thermal protection against the Moon's extreme temperatures!
luna_te_bajaste: Boots on lunar soil! You got off the moon buggy.
luna_suelo_junto: You're next to the orange soil!
luna_suelo_bajate: Get off the moon buggy and collect samples!
luna_suelo_manten: Hold your fist closed to collect samples!
cine_despegue_ultimo_trabajo: The moon buggy has one last mission! Thanks to its camera, the liftoff of the last two astronauts to walk on the Moon was recorded, after taking them much farther.
cine_despegue_operador: Imagine this! From Earth, an operator controlled the moon buggy's camera to follow the liftoff.
cine_despegue_solo: The moon buggy stayed there, alone in the silence of the Moon! It wasn't abandoned: it fulfilled an extraordinary mission. A great success for NASA and for humanity.
luna_despegue_libre: The astronauts have already left, but you can stay a little longer! Explore the valley, follow the moon buggy's tracks and, when you're ready, hold your fist closed to return to the museum.
luna_despegue_libre_teclado: The astronauts have already left, but you can stay a little longer! Explore the valley, follow the moon buggy's tracks and, when you're ready, hold down the E key to return to the museum.
vitrina_lrv_teclado: Can you imagine driving a car on the Moon? This is the moon buggy {directo}, the Apollo 17 lunar vehicle. In 1972 {exacto} the astronauts used it to explore the surface, and it's still there, more than 50 years later! Do you want to discover its story {cercano}? Press space to start the interaction!
luna_mision_cumplida: You did it, explorer! Mission accomplished!
luna_mision_salida: Hold your fist closed to return to the museum, explorer!
luna_mision_salida_teclado: Hold down the E key to return to the museum, explorer!
pieza_larguero_funcion: Longitudinal aluminum tube beam that carries the vehicle's load. The chassis was 2219 aluminum, in three sections.
pieza_aligeramiento_funcion: Dark cut-out that saves weight in the rail (shape from the model).
pieza_celosia_funcion: Tube that stiffens the frame without adding much weight (layout from the model).
pieza_bisagra_funcion: Joint that let the chassis fold so it could ride in the lunar module bay.
pieza_travesano_funcion: Transverse tube that joins the two side rails.
pieza_piso_funcion: Forms the chassis floor (its exact design is approximate in this model).
pieza_malla_funcion: Woven zinc-coated steel strands, 0.083 cm thick, that work as the tire: the wheel holds no air.
pieza_chevrones_funcion: V-shaped plate on the mesh that gives grip; it covered 50% of the contact area.
pieza_ruedaCubo_funcion: Central spun-aluminum part that joins the wheel to the axle and the motor.
pieza_ruedaAroAluminio_funcion: Formed aluminum rim that the mesh is attached to.
pieza_ruedaInterior_funcion: Dark backing of the tread, seen through the mesh (shape from the model).
pieza_ruedaDisco_funcion: Mesh flank that joins the rim to the hub (shape from the model).
pieza_ruedaNervio_funcion: Rod that stiffens the wheel flank (shape from the model).
pieza_ruedaAro_funcion: Ring that holds the edges of the mesh (shape from the model).
pieza_ruedaPerno_funcion: Fastens the rim to the wheel (number and shape from the model).
pieza_motorTraccion_funcion: 0.25 hp DC electric motor that turns a single wheel: there is one per wheel.
pieza_cajaArmonica_funcion: Reduces the motor's turns with an 80:1 ratio to give the wheel more force.
pieza_brazoDireccion_funcion: Joins the suspension to the hub and points the wheel when turning (shape from the model).
pieza_horquilla_funcion: V-shaped arm of the double horizontal wishbone: it holds the wheel to the chassis and lets it move up and down.
pieza_barraTorsion_funcion: Bar that works as a spring: it twists when the wheel rises and brings it back.
pieza_guardabarros_funcion: Cover over the wheel that holds back the dust it kicks up ("dust guards" in the NSSDC).
pieza_extensionGuardabarros_funcion: Extends the fender forward and backward (shape from the model).
pieza_bordeGuardabarros_funcion: Dark trim on the fender lip (shape from the model).
pieza_rielGuardabarros_funcion: Dark guide the extensions slide along (shape from the model).
pieza_remache_funcion: Joins the rail to the fender (number and shape from the model).
pieza_soporteGuardabarros_funcion: Tube that holds the fender to the chassis (shape from the model).
pieza_bandera_funcion: Decoration of the model on the fender side; not confirmed by NASA.
pieza_asientoLona_funcion: Nylon webbing stretched where the astronaut sits.
pieza_asientoMarco_funcion: Foldable aluminum tube that holds the webbing.
pieza_asientoRespaldo_funcion: Nylon strap that forms the seat backrest.
pieza_asidero_funcion: Tube to hold on to when getting on and off (shape from the model).
pieza_cinturon_funcion: Velcro belt that holds the astronaut to the seat.
pieza_reposapies_funcion: Adjustable platform where the astronaut rests their feet.
pieza_reposabrazos_funcion: Support between the two seats, next to the controller.
pieza_mandoBase_funcion: Boot and box that hold the T-handle (shape from the model).
pieza_mando_funcion: Lever between the seats: forward drives, left and right turn, and back brakes.
pieza_interruptor_funcion: Switched on at the handle before pulling back, to go in reverse.
pieza_placaInterruptor_funcion: Mount of the reverse switch (shape from the model).
pieza_consolaSoporte_funcion: Tubes that hold the console above the chassis (shape from the model).
pieza_consola_funcion: Box that gathers the driver's instruments (approximate layout).
pieza_consolaPanel_funcion: Plate that holds the indicators and switches (approximate layout).
pieza_consolaInstrumento_funcion: Shows data to the driver; NASA describes a gyro and an odometer, but not this layout.
pieza_consolaInterruptor_funcion: Switch in the top row of the panel (function still to be confirmed).
pieza_panelPotencia_funcion: Group of switches for drive power (columns still to be verified).
pieza_panelDireccion_funcion: Group of steering switches (columns still to be verified).
pieza_panelHabilitar_funcion: Group of switches that enable the drive (columns still to be verified).
pieza_consolaEmpunadura_funcion: Handle on each side of the panel (shape from the model).
pieza_sombraSolar_funcion: Gives a heading by hand using the Sun's shadow.
pieza_baterias_funcion: One of the two 36 V, 121 Ah silver-zinc non-rechargeable batteries that power the vehicle.
pieza_electronica_funcion: Box with the control electronics (its exact contents are still to be confirmed).
pieza_cable_funcion: Carries power or signals between units (routing from the model).
pieza_lcru_funcion: Relays communications to Earth; it is wrapped in gold foil.
pieza_asaLCRU_funcion: Handle for moving the communications unit (shape from the model).
pieza_panelLCRU_funcion: Control panel of the communications unit (shape from the model).
pieza_camaraCuerpo_funcion: The vehicle's television camera, wrapped in gold foil; it is powered from the LRV outlet.
pieza_camaraPedestal_funcion: Mount that raises the camera (shape from the model).
pieza_camaraControl_funcion: White box under the camera (contents still to be confirmed).
pieza_camaraLente_funcion: Lens where the image comes in (shape from the model).
pieza_antenaMalla_funcion: Large mesh dish that points at Earth to send television and data.
pieza_antenaMastil_funcion: Holds the antenna at the front of the vehicle.
pieza_antenaNervadura_funcion: Rod that holds the dish mesh (number and shape from the model).
pieza_antenaCubo_funcion: Central part of the dish (shape from the model).
pieza_antenaAlimentador_funcion: Pointing rod with the antenna feed (shape from the model).
pieza_antenaBaja_funcion: Auxiliary antenna of white tube (details still to be confirmed).
pieza_portaCaja_funcion: Rear box for carrying tools and samples (still to be confirmed).
pieza_portaPerforacion_funcion: Round cap of the rear box (shape from the model).
pieza_cajaMuestras_funcion: Box to store lunar samples (still to be confirmed).
pieza_portaMarco_funcion: Tubes that frame the tool carrier (shape from the model).
pieza_pinzas_funcion: Tool to pick up rocks without bending down (still to be confirmed).
pieza_sinNombre_funcion: Part without a confirmed name: still to be identified.
modos_pista: Point at an option and Robi will tell you what it's about. Once you've picked it, clap or press space to enter.
modo_historia_desc: Learn its story and live the mission on the Moon
modo_taller_desc: Explore the parts of the moon buggy in 3D, piece by piece
modo_libre_desc: Drive the moon buggy and roam the Moon at your own pace
modos_robi_intro: Great, {nombre}! Point at the option you prefer and I'll tell you what it's about.
modos_robi_historia: Moon Buggy Story: you'll know the lunar vehicle, drive the LRV across the Moon and collect a sample of the orange soil.
modos_robi_taller: 3D Workshop: you'll see the moon buggy on a white background. Press D and it comes apart piece by piece.
modos_robi_libre: Free Exploration: drive the moon buggy across the lunar valley, with no mission and no rush.
modos_robi_libre_teclado: Free Exploration: drive the moon buggy across the lunar valley, with no mission and no rush.
libre_bienvenida: The moon buggy is all yours, {nombre}! Hold the wheel with both hands and raise your knees to drive, and make the OK gesture with both hands to get off. To get back on, clap hard. Explore the Moon at your own pace and, when you want to go back to the museum, keep your fist closed.
libre_bienvenida_teclado: The moon buggy is all yours, {nombre}! Use W, A, S and D to drive and B to get off. To get back on, press space. Explore the Moon at your own pace and, when you want to go back to the museum, hold down the E key.
taller_pendiente: Still to be confirmed with NASA
